profile.owner: WorkWave LLC. EQT funds have held WorkWave as a standalone portfolio company since June 2021, after it separated from IFS, which bought it in 2017. Sister brands: RealGreen (lawn) and TEAM Software (WinTeam, Lighthouse).
profile.target_customers: Pest control operators from small to enterprise, focused on mid-size and large multi-branch residential and commercial companies. The vendor claims it processes about 70% of PCT Top 100 revenue. Named users include Terminix, Truly Nolen and Arrow (third-party data). Capterra reviewers are mostly small businesses.
profile.pricing: Not published. Quote-based Small Business, Professional and Enterprise packages, with many features gated by tier. Third-party estimates: about $100 per user per month, setup fees around $1,500, annual auto-renewing contracts with 3 to 5% yearly increases. Extra notification credits are billed separately, and payment processing rates depend on volume.
profile.deployment: Cloud. Browser web app (PestPac Desktop) on Windows or macOS, modernized in March 2024, plus native mobile apps. Releases ship every two weeks.
profile.mobile_app: PestPac Mobile (version 3) for iOS and Android (64-bit devices, latest OS plus two prior versions). Rated 2.4 from 148 ratings on the US App Store. Classic Mobile and Mobile 2 are retired.
integrations: WorkWave Payments (native card, ACH, Apple Pay, Samsung Pay)
Voice for Pest phone system; Dialpad and TalkDesk via API
Azuga, Linxup and Verizon Connect telematics
Bell smart traps and other smart trap hardware
Wisetack (Pay Over Time consumer financing) and YouLend (WorkWave Capital)
Wavelytics Data Factory Snowflake share for Power BI or Tableau
strengths: Deep pest-specific tooling: termite WDI and NPMA-33 forms, Sentricon reporting, IPM device scanning, multi-unit buildings and smart traps.
Strong chemical tracking with built-in state reports (California, Arizona, New York) and inventory tracked from warehouse to truck.
Built for enterprise scale: RouteOp optimizes a month of routes, plus multi-branch, an API and adoption by large national operators.
Mobile app works fully offline, covering forms, signatures, materials and field payments.
Integrated payments and fintech: card updater, consumer financing and capital loans.
weaknesses: Reviewers call pricing high and opaque, citing costly modules, setup fees and long auto-renewing contracts.
The interface is complicated and dated, with a steep learning curve for admins and staff.
Reviewers report persistent bugs and slow support when issues need escalation.
The mobile app is rated 2.4 on the App Store, and some users report unreliable camera barcode scanning.
There is no built-in general ledger. QuickBooks is fed by a GL export, and users report reconciliation discrepancies.
profile.wisconsin_notes: No Wisconsin customers, forms or ATCP 29 support found. The vendor names only California, Arizona and New York state reports plus generic state-specific exports. Third-party data says its customer base skews to the Southeast and California.

features.notes: Sales Center tracks leads and opportunities through funnels with auto-assignment and expected revenue. Lead Management appears only in Professional and Enterprise packages.
Reporting includes lead source and marketing campaign performance reports; CallTrackingMetrics and Google Analytics integrations support campaign ROI.
Branded proposals can offer several service levels and price points per contact via Digital Forms, which is listed from the Professional package up.
Customers review and sign proposals and contracts digitally; agreements can be sent for signature after inspections. Digital Forms is a Professional package item.
Sales Center field app offers territory maps with property data, knock status tracking, agreement creation and payment capture at the door.
A Commissions report exists and professional services map commission structures into PestPac; holds or chargebacks on early cancellation are not documented.
Marketing Automation sends email campaigns and drip sequences to upsell customers; Professional package and up. SMS campaigns not documented.
No cancellation reason codes or save workflows found; only canceled appointment reports and Account Updater for card-related churn.
Supports parent and child billing hierarchies for complex commercial accounts, and commercial portal users manage multiple locations and accounts.
Voice for Pest partner integration pops customer info on incoming calls and records calls; Dialpad and TalkDesk connect via API.
Recurring services support weekly, biweekly, monthly, quarterly and nth weekday patterns, with default schedules per service type.
No documentation found for a fixed number of service rounds within a seasonal date window.
Proposal templates hold service levels, materials and price points set by branch or division; pricing by property size is not documented.
Accounting module lets operators execute price increases on their own schedule; mechanics of the mass update are not detailed publicly.
A Renewals report exists, but term length, auto-renewal and early cancellation fee fields are not documented.
Termite module manages inspections and renewals and a Renewals report exists; warranty records and automatic renewal billing reminders are not described.
No callback logging documented in core PestPac; Wavelytics is said to flag callback spikes, and cost capture is undocumented.
Recurring services generate appointments from set frequencies, and RouteOp can optimize a full month of routes at once.
Appointment scheduler shows technicians by hour with drag and drop moves, plus map and calendar views of routes.
RouteOp optimizes hundreds of orders across daily, weekly or monthly routes; Small Business gets basic routing, optimization starts at Professional.
Technicians carry skill types such as termite license or wildlife trapping; RouteOp and the scheduler block or warn on unqualified assignments.
CustomerConnect lets customers request service appointments and order services online; true self-scheduling into open slots is not documented.
App tracks technician location without extra hardware, with a live Vehicle Map, Closest Tech, and Azuga or Verizon telematics integration.
RouteOp redistributes a technician's jobs for vacations or sick calls; weather-driven mass rescheduling is not documented.
PestPac Mobile (version 3) for iOS and Android; App Store rating 2.4 from 148 ratings.
Technicians complete work orders, log materials, take payments, fill forms and capture signatures offline, syncing on reconnect.
Technicians pick chemicals from a preset list with method, rate and quantity; EPA numbers auto-populate and unit thresholds limit entries.
App captures photos, diagrams, comments, documents and customer signatures at job completion.
Phone camera works as a barcode scanner for bait stations and devices; Socket S700 and S800 external scanners are supported.
Accepts cash, check, card and ACH in the field, shows unpaid invoices, and offers Pay Over Time financing.
App records time in and out of jobs and shows timesheets; a Timecards report supports payroll.
Materials used are deducted from truck inventory automatically; whether technicians can view or adjust truck stock on the device is not documented.
Visit records capture product, EPA number, target, method, rate and quantity, feeding state material reports.
Chemical list stores EPA registration numbers and concentrations; SDS sits in the commercial portal library, and label documents are not mentioned.
Scheduler warns when a technician lacks required licensing and forms pull license details; license expiry alerts are not documented.
Built-in California material and Cal-Ag reports, New York material reports, Arizona TARF, plus other state-specific compliance exports.
Automated reminders and emailed service reports exist, but no dedicated pre-application pesticide notice or registry notification feature is documented.
No restricted-use pesticide controls or RUP record fields found; only per-chemical quantity thresholds and skill-based assignment.
Tracks stock from distributor to warehouse to truck, with transfers, returns, distributor file imports, cost export and expected usage reports.
Vendor names California, Arizona and New York reports only; no Wisconsin ATCP 29, landscape registry or posting support found.
IPM module manages devices per area with camera or Bluetooth scanning; IPM and Multi-Unit support start at the Professional package.
Technicians draw device locations, multi-unit floor plan schematics locate devices, and the portal maps devices. Professional package and up.
Commercial portal offers graphical trend reports and heat maps by area, date or pest; Logbook trend logs need Professional or higher.
Logbook organizes inspection reports, sighting logs and licenses with auditor-only access; Auditor Reports are Enterprise only. AIB, SQF, BRC not named.
CustomerConnect+ gives commercial clients inspection reports, device floor plan maps, SDS sheets and compliance certificates online; labels not listed.
Customers log sightings that create service tickets and track open conditions and IPM recommendations; part of Logbook, Professional package and up.
Invoice consolidation and parent and child billing hierarchies exist; PO numbers and net terms are not documented.
Grid and aerial sketches with footage measurement, Sentricon bait station scanning and reporting, and WDI, WDO and NPMA-33 forms on mobile.
Wildlife trapping appears only as a technician skill type; no multi-visit trapping or exclusion job tooling is documented.
No bed bug job workflows or customer prep checklists found.
No mosquito or tick program features documented.
WorkWave Payments built in with card, ACH, Apple Pay and Samsung Pay; WorkWave acts as its own payment facilitator.
Credit card auto-billing charges stored cards after service, and Account Updater refreshes expired or replaced cards.
Supports recurring invoicing, bulk monthly billing, prepayment and annual discounts, and payment plans billed at chosen frequencies.
Avalara is a listed tax compliance partner; native tax reporting considers state rules, but per-address rate lookup is not documented.
Collections manager moves past-due accounts through stages, builds call lists, sends notices and exports to collection agencies; late fees not documented.
Offers invoice consolidation plus Invoices and Statements reports.
No documentation found on prorated refunds or balances due when agreements are cancelled.
Vendor describes exporting to an external general ledger package such as QuickBooks; AR and period lockdown exist, but no double-entry GL.
GL export file is imported into QuickBooks on your own schedule, not a live sync; GL Export is a Professional package item.
Generic general ledger export can feed other accounting packages; no named Sage, Xero or NetSuite connector found.
Prepayment discounts exist, but deferred revenue recognition as visits are performed is not documented.
Reports cover service-line profitability and inventory cost export; per-job labor and material margin is not documented.
Technician Production and Timecards reports support payroll; no named payroll integration or production-pay calculation found.
CustomerConnect portal: pay by card or ACH, store payment methods, view service and inspection history and invoices, request service, chat.
Call, text or email reminders and on-my-way alerts; Customer Communications is listed from the Professional package, and extra notification credits cost more.
Communication Center provides two-way SMS and MMS with recorded conversations; part of Customer Communications, Professional package and up.
Online Reviews automates collection, letting technicians request reviews right after service and staff respond to reviews.
Inspection and service reports are emailed or printed from the field or after posting; materials are tracked on service orders.
Standard reports include AR aging with as-of dates, sales by month, collections, payment register, material and service completion.
Canceled appointment and Renewals reports exist, but retention or churn rates by route, technician or service are not documented.
Technician Production, Timecards, schedule-to-actual and Route Comparison reports cover technician output.
Report Writer and Custom Reporting come with Professional and up; Wavelytics Data Factory, a separately purchased Snowflake share, feeds Power BI or Tableau.
Multi-Branch appears only in the Enterprise package; reports can filter by branch.
A third-party review reports configurable user access roles, and portal auditor users can be limited by location; no vendor documentation found.
PestPac Cloud API covers scheduling, billing and payments with webhooks; API Integrations listed only in the Enterprise package.
Data Services team with an analyst runs migrations from many systems, including a standard FieldRoutes script; a free CSV import utility is also offered.
Communication Center offers AI interaction summaries (Professional package and up); WAIve assistant and agents announced for the WorkWave suite from Q2 2026.
WorkWave-hosted Website Builder with lead forms feeding PestPac, per-branch domains and SEO metadata, for a separate monthly fee.
WorkWave Print Marketing (postcards, lawn signs, QR attribution) is a separate product; call tracking via CallTrackingMetrics; basic SEO in website builder.

extra_features.notes: Bluetooth or Wi-Fi smart traps (Bell and others) report rodent activity from 50 to 100 feet away and update service records.
Bulk setup of units and areas, with per-unit devices, treatments, skipped areas, signatures and unit reports.
Automatic monthly Sentricon submissions plus Phase II stewardship and average station spacing reports.
Suggests technicians for new or emergency jobs by distance and added drive time.
Pay Over Time via Wisetack for $500 to $25,000 jobs in office or app; WorkWave Capital loans via YouLend.
Refreshes expired or replaced stored cards automatically to cut involuntary churn; vendor says no extra charge.
Stops transactions from posting into closed accounting periods.
Projects chemical needs from scheduled jobs; distributor transaction files can be imported into inventory.
Map pins show square footage, beds, baths and nearby existing customers to prequalify door-to-door prospects.
Residential customer feedback surveys listed as a PestPac solution.
Customers chat with agents in the portal, and operators can show marketing messages and promotions there.
Industry KPI benchmarking, role-based scorecards and AskWAIve natural-language questions; marked coming soon.
24/7 learning system, PestPac University webinars and community included with base licenses.
